parts.label: (a)
parts.text: For any point outside a spherical conductor, the charge on the sphere may be considered to act as a point charge at its centre. By reference to electric field lines, explain this.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
An isolated spherical conductor has charge $q$, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1}}

Fig. 6.1

Point P is a movable point that, at any one time, is a distance $x$ from the centre of the sphere.

The variation with distance $x$ of the electric potential $V$ at point P due to the charge on the sphere is shown in Fig. 6.2.

{{figure:figure_6_2}}

Fig. 6.2

Use Fig. 6.2 to determine
parts.text: the electric field strength $E$ at point P where $x = 6.0\text{ cm}$,

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the radius $R$ of the sphere. Explain your answer.
